PARSECOVE

About & methods

A little transparency goes a long way.

A small toolbox for everyday work.

ParseCove brings everyday developer utilities into one place: Unix timestamp conversion, CSS PX/REM conversion, Base64 text encoding and decoding, a URL-safe Base64URL tool with hex output, and separate entry points for image encoding and decoding.

How calculations work

Time inputs are validated before conversion. Whole timestamps are parsed with integer arithmetic and displayed with JavaScript Date and Intl. Base64 follows the standard and URL-safe alphabets in RFC 4648. Text is interpreted as UTF-8. Images are inspected by byte signatures and decoded by your browser. PX/REM conversion uses an explicit root font size and selected rounding precision.

Limits are part of the result.

Each tool explains its assumptions and restrictions. Timestamp auto-detection is a heuristic. Timezone results depend on your browser’s timezone database. Image preview supports PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP up to 10 MB. CSS conversion uses standard JavaScript numbers and supports numeric values, not whole stylesheets.

Free, focused and local.

No account is required by the tools. The app has no paid features, input uploads, or third-party analytics. You can inspect the source code and conversion tests on GitHub.

Built for the little things that slow you down.
